searched: Searched (2026-10-15) for founding and leadership announcements and the 2024–2025 licensing-and-hiring arrangements of Inflection AI, Character.AI, Adept and Windsurf (Codeium), and Microsoft AI. Retrieved: Microsoft's 19 March 2024 blog post; Greylock's 8 March 2022 launch post by Mustafa Suleyman; Inflection's own blog (March 2023 PBC post, May 2024 post by Sean White, July 2026 press release); the UK CMA's Microsoft/Inflection case page and phase 1 summary decision; Character.AI's blog (Dec 2022 'Introducing Character', Dec 2024 CTO post, June 2025 CEO post); Adept's April 2022 launch post and June 2024 update (relay); Amazon Science's December 2024 AGI SF Lab post; Windsurf's July 2025 post (relay; direct TLS connection reset); the April 2025 rename post now hosted on devin.ai; Cognition's 14 July 2025 post; Disney's 18 September 2026 press release; and reporting from TechCrunch (2 Aug 2024, 29 Aug 2024) and The Verge (11 Jul 2025). Retrieval failures: Inflection's March 2024 'The new Inflection' post (inflection.ai/blog/the-new-inflection and inflection.ai/the-new-inflection both 404); Character.AI's August 2024 post on the Google agreement (blog.character.ai/our-next-phase-of-growth/ 404; not in the blog sitemap), so the Character.AI–Google agreement rests on TechCrunch reporting that quotes the post and the parties' statements; no Google primary statement on Windsurf was retrieved (Google's statement is quoted in The Verge); no Amazon announcement of the June 2024 Adept arrangement was found; the Internet Archive is unreachable. Search engines were used only to discover URLs. Not drafted: the Google DeepMind roles of Noam Shazeer, Daniel De Freitas, Varun Mohan and Douglas Chen (left to the Google pass); Character.AI's founding date (no retrieved primary source states it); Adept's founding date (only 'two-and-a-half years ago' in June 2024); the Exafunction-to-Codeium rename in 2022 (stated in the April 2025 post but would need an extra historical-name entity); Character.AI's 12 October 2026 announcement of a voluntary Chapter 11 process for a court-supervised sale (no fitting predicate; coordinator may decide); the later careers of Ashish Vaswani and Niki Parmar after Adept; COO/CPO appointments (outside the executive scope).

claims.subject: microsoft
claims.statement: The UK Competition and Markets Authority stated in the summary of its phase 1 decision (published on 4 September 2024) that Microsoft had announced on 19 March 2024 the hiring of former Inflection employees amounting, in the CMA's understanding, to almost all of Inflection's team, and that Microsoft had entered into arrangements with Inflection including a non-exclusive licence to use Inflection IP.

time.note: Date on which, according to the CMA, Microsoft announced the hiring; the dates of the licence and other arrangements are not given in the summary.

claims.qualification: The licensing element rests on the CMA's phase 1 summary decision; 4 September 2024 is its publication date on GOV.UK, and the summary text itself carries no date. Inflection's own March 2024 announcement could not be retrieved and Microsoft's announcement does not mention a licence. The CMA describes the hiring as having taken place and the arrangements as entered into, so the record carries no 'announced' stage; it does not give the dates of the licence or other arrangements. Under UK merger law the CMA treated the arrangements as the acquisition of certain assets of Inflection forming a relevant merger situation, and cleared it; that is a legal characterisation, not a statement that Microsoft acquired Inflection AI as a company. Terms and payments are not recorded here.

evidence.passage: On 19 March 2024, Microsoft announced that it had hired several former Inflection employees, which the CMA understands amounted to almost all of Inflection’s team
Microsoft also entered into a series of arrangements with Inflection including, among others, a nonexclusive licensing deal to utilise Inflection IP in a range of ways.
is a relevant merger situation falling within the merger control jurisdiction of the CMA
Several members of the Inflection team have chosen to join Mustafa and Karén at Microsoft.

claims.subject: google
claims.statement: Windsurf announced on 11 July 2025 an agreement with Google under which Varun, Douglas and some members of its R&D team would join Google; The Verge reported the same day that Google would take a non-exclusive licence to some of Windsurf's technology.

time.note: Announcement date; signing and effective dates not stated.

claims.qualification: Windsurf’s own post states the agreement and the hires but not the licence. The licence and Google’s lack of control or stake rest on The Verge’s reporting of the Google–Windsurf announcement; the Google spokesperson statement quoted there does not mention the licence. No Google primary statement was retrieved. Terms and payments are not recorded here.

evidence.passage: Google will not have any control over nor a stake in Windsurf, but it will take a non-exclusive license to some of Windsurf’s technology.
Google will instead hire Windsurf CEO Varun Mohan, cofounder Douglas Chen, and some of Windsurf’s R&D employees
As part of the agreement, Varun, Douglas, and some members of our R&D team will join Google.
